summary: Three new dependencies and two ownership overlaps, following a catalogue-wide summary/scope screen and primary-stage checks for the retained pairs. Multiquadratic supplies the existing square-class prefix to QuadraticFormInvariants, and the degree/Galois and splitting computations for ClassFieldTheory's displayed biquadratic counterexample. Those example-only inputs do not depend on genus theory or global reciprocity. The overlaps separate the shared unit-square bound from quadratic genus theory and the general narrow-class carrier from its quadratic application. Existing NumberFieldArithmetic/Frobenius and ClassFieldTheory/Hilbert-class-field pairs are not duplicated. A real-place inconsistency in the source is recorded for correction. This is a link proposal, not implementation or mathematical approval.

links.reason: The consumer explicitly imports the Multiquadratic square-class language. The supplied prefix is the additive quotient, its ZMod 2 structure, and independence versus nonempty-subset products; the consumer adds multiplicative notation, field-map and cardinality adapters. This is not dependence on tower degree, Galois classification or genus theory. The prefix already exists at the pinned Tau Ceti baseline: reuse it, do not reimplement it. The quotient and independence equivalence hold over any field; characteristic restrictions belong to their subsequent applications.

links.reason: Example-only dependency: the displayed obstruction to lifting H² classes uses L=Q(sqrt(13),sqrt(17)) of degree four with elementary-abelian Galois group. Instantiate the independent two-radicand theorem: 13, 17 and 221 are nonsquares, as their prime valuations show. Positive radicands make all embeddings real. This supplies the finite extension and its group, not the Brauer/idele cohomology computation. The general construction of globalInv does not depend on this example, and neither genus fields nor ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 may be used as inputs to Layer 10.

links.reason: Example-only dependency: Layer 10 needs 13 to split in Q(sqrt(17)) and 17 in Q(sqrt(13)). Apply the singleton odd-prime splitting criterion, with square witnesses 2²=17 mod 13 and 8²=13 mod 17. Do not apply the two-radicand away-from-ramification formula at either ramified prime of the full compositum. Together with the degree-four/exponent-two group, quadratic discriminants and the separately owned completion/ramification dictionary, these computations bound local decomposition groups by two. At other finite primes the extension is unramified and its decomposition group is cyclic; at infinity it is totally real. The edge supplies only this arithmetic part, not H² of idele classes or a proof that 25 fails to be a global norm.

EffectiveBounds Layer 1 states [O_F^×:(O_F^×)^2] <= 2^[F:Q]; Multiquadratic Layer 2 lists the same unit-square input, and its migration-source section explicitly calls the port shared with EffectiveBounds.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the number-field unit-square bound with EffectiveBounds and its generic group helper in shared algebra. Multiquadratic consumes that theorem while retaining its ambiguous-class formula and elementary-two class-group quotient. The exponent [F:Q] is not the number of ramified primes. No merger or duplicate port is needed.

overlaps.detail: GlobalNumberFields Layer 2 constructs the general narrow class group, the map to the ordinary group and its unit-sign kernel; Multiquadratic Layer 3 also claims the narrow-class definition. The common carrier is the ray class group with trivial finite modulus and all real places.
overlaps.proposal: GlobalNumberFields owns the carrier, comparison map and kernel; Multiquadratic owns the quadratic specialization and genus-field/elementary-two-quotient calculations. Correct the real-place inconsistency before equating the ordinary genus field with the full prime-discriminant compositum: for discriminant 12=(-4)(-3), that compositum contains i and complexifies the real places of Q(sqrt(3)). Scope the full compositum to the narrow convention (or imaginary fields); the ordinary real case needs the real-place restriction. Source files are not changed by this packet.
